elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "HDI shall defend and indemnify the Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim" — express defence duty running to the Company and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same sentence extends indemnity to "the Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or the Site infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — the Site is the deliverable under this development/hosting agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data caused by HDI".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "The Company shall indemnify HDI against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of the Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law" — two narrow limbs only, no defence obligation added against us.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) of the inserted indemnity covers third-party allegations of IP infringement or misappropriation by the Services or the Site.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-modification exclusion was inserted, so the condition does not apply and the position (which merely tolerates such an exclusion) is not breached.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted, which is more favourable to us than the fallback tolerates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion inserted, so nothing to test.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no procure/modify/replace remedy mechanic for an infringement finding.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure-of-remedies language appears in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No monetary super-cap (3× annual fees) is stated; the indemnity is uncapped in the inserted text.

reasons: Every preferred element is met in the operative inserted text: mutual-but-asymmetric indemnity with HDI defending and indemnifying the Company and its affiliates for IP infringement, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice, control and cooperation, and a Company indemnity confined to Company-provided Content and its own breach of law. The preferred level is position-complete, so the fallback gaps (procure/modify/replace, refund, 3× super-cap) do not need repair.

Minimality holds: this is a concise insertion into a document with no indemnity anywhere, no existing language is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense, additional procedures or boilerplate) were added; the damages/costs/fees phrase is core to the indemnify-against-claims element rather than a bolt-on damages category.
Intent preserved: the Globix acknowledgement in 9(b) and Section 10 survive unchanged and the new paragraph creates no contradiction with the warranty or liability mechanics.

Drafting nit to tighten (not a level failure): the rendered paragraph is unnumbered although the rationale describes it as "Section 9A" — give it an express number (e.g. 9A or a new Section 10 with renumbering) so it is not read as a sub-part of Section 9 (Warranties).

Confirm that "Services" and "Content" are defined or used elsewhere in the Agreement; if either is not a defined term, replace with the contract's own wording (e.g. the services described in Section 1, and content supplied by the Company) to avoid a dangling term.
